regions.region: page 1 title, author block, abstract, and article metadata
regions.finding: Verified the full source title and the aggregate claim that Cu6 nanoclusters catalyze open-air protosilylation of alkynes, alkenes, and simple enynes. This is article-level context, not an experiment-specific yield.

regions.region: page 1 Introduction and prior ligand-promoted protosilylation discussion
regions.finding: Classified earlier alkyne/en­yne protosilylation as cited prior work and the new Cu6 system as the current generic platform; the actual Scheme 1 drawings occur on page 2.

regions.region: page 1 lower-right beginning of Results and Discussion
regions.finding: The page introduces a two-step Cu6 synthesis but the operational quantities continue on page 2. Concrete precursor/Cu6 records use page-2 evidence; no truncated page-1 quantity was invented.

unresolved: Page 1 gives only aggregate claims and an incomplete lead-in to the catalyst synthesis.
No workspace Supporting Information association is established.

regions.finding: Visually separated two prior-literature reaction classes from the current cluster platform. Generic R/EWG drawings and catalyst ranges were not promoted to concrete current-paper runs.
Recorded [Cu(MeCN)4]BF4/tBuSH/MeCN/NEt3 charges, room-temperature 12 h reaction, filtration/washes/ambient drying, yellow powder, and 90% yield as one ordered experiment.

Recorded the common 6 mL MeCN/CHCl3 charge, 10 min pre-stir, sequential Na2mnt/NaBH4 additions, 12 h reaction, and 48 h dark evaporation. Cu6-1 gives 61%; Cu6-2 is the explicit dppe-for-dppm variant with no printed yield.
Crystal/ESI-MS/SCXRD information characterizes the two catalyst-preparation products and does not define additional synthesis experiments or verify machine structures.

unresolved: Cu6 reaction/crystallization temperatures and atmosphere are not printed; Cu6-2 yield is absent.
Figure S1 is mentioned but no SI association was inferred.

regions.region: page 3 upper/right Table 1 reaction header, entries 1–20, and footnotes a–d
regions.finding: Recorded all 20 rows independently with the shared 0.30 mmol phenylacetylene/1.1 equiv silylboronate/0.1 mol% Cu6-1/1.1 equiv DBU/MeCN-MeOH/air/room-temperature/8 h conditions, row replacements/omissions, footnote-d 5 mol% salt loading, NMR yields, and TONs. Dashes were not converted to zero.

Mapped catalyst/base necessity and Cu6-2 comparison to their existing table rows. Table 1 entry 1 is merged with the identical Table 2 product-1 run, retaining 91% crude-NMR and 90% isolated yields separately.

regions.region: page 3 Figure 2 and catalyst packing discussion
regions.finding: Packing/structure graphics characterize Cu6-1/Cu6-2 and support catalyst rationale; they do not create reaction records.

unresolved: Optimization workup, purification, masses, detection limits, and replacement-solvent absolute volumes are not reported.
The chemical correctness of compact catalyst structures remains unverified.

regions.region: page 4 upper-left continuation of optimization discussion
regions.finding: Linked Cu cluster/salt/base/solvent comparisons to Table 1 rows 4–20 without duplicating prose summaries.

regions.region: page 4 Table 2 reaction header, products 1–23, and footnotes a–e
regions.finding: Visually recorded every scope result. Product 1 is merged with Table 1 entry 1; products 2–23 are distinct records with isolated yields, shared >20:1 rr except product 12 at 2.2:1, and row-specific 0.2 mol%, 12 h, or NaOtBu overrides.
Mapped products 1–23, the unassociated Table S7 additive series, two later page-5 scale-ups, ten Scheme 2 derivatizations, and equation-2 disilylation to their records without importing SI-only rows.
Linked the reported eight-run Cu6-1 retention and Cu6-2 decline to two Figure 3a recycling-series records. Individual chart yields were not estimated.

unresolved: Table 2 omits row workups, purifications, masses, and exact names for compact depicted structures.
Table S7 individual additive rows and numerical recoveries are unavailable because SI association is unestablished.
Recycling per-run operating details and exact yields are not printed.

regions.finding: Recorded the independent 6.0 mmol phenylacetylene/1.1 equiv PhMe2SiBpin/0.005 mol% Cu6-1/MeCN-MeOH/DBU/air/room-temperature/60 h scale-up giving product 1 in 71% and TON 14200.

regions.region: page 5 Scheme 2 central preparation and arrows i–x
regions.finding: Recorded the 10 mmol standard-condition preparation of 2.2 g product 1 in 94%, plus ten independent derivatizations to products 24–32 and 19 with every printed reagent/catalyst, solvent, temperature, time, and yield.
Recorded the distinct 2.1-equiv double protosilylation to E-disilylated 33 in 84%; it is not merged with Table 2 monosilylated allene 23.
Linked the no-effect TEMPO controls and three deuterated-solvent/atmosphere runs to Figure 3c/d records on page 6. SI Table S8 details beyond the printed percentages were not imported.
Classified A–D and TS-1–TS-3 as a plausible DFT-supported mechanism; they are not isolated preparations.

unresolved: Scale-up and Scheme 2 arrows omit multiple absolute reagent charges, workups, purifications, masses, atmospheres, and yield bases.
TEMPO/deuterium analytical bases and SI Table S8 details are not available.
Mechanistic intermediates are proposed and unquantified.

regions.finding: Visually inspected both Cu6-1 and Cu6-2 eight-run bar series. Because exact bar labels are absent, no numerical heights were estimated; only the explicit prose trend is retained.
Linked before/after-catalysis UV–Vis characterization to the existing Cu6-1 recycling record. It is catalyst-stability evidence, not a new synthetic reaction.
Recorded 1- and 3-equiv TEMPO controls as distinct rows, each 91% yield. The 0-equiv/91% row corresponds to the standard Table 1 entry 1 and was not duplicated.
Recorded all three solvent/atmosphere rows independently with Da/Db values: <1/<1, 67/17, and 77/27 percent.

regions.finding: Recorded one mechanism record with ordered A–D/TS-1–TS-3 labels and printed barriers 17.9, 23.1, and 20.5 kcal mol−1; proposed entities were not treated as experiments.
